overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for debating four measures. They are the yearly spending bill for military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs for the budget year starting October 2025 (H.R. 3944), a bill requiring the Homeland Security Department to publish monthly counts of "special interest aliens" (people flagged as possible security risks) caught trying to cross the border illegally (H.R. 275), a bill making noncitizens convicted of or who committed drunk or impaired driving barred from entry and subject to deportation (H.R. 875), and a resolution condemning the June 2025 riots in Los Angeles (H. Res. 516). For each, it limits debate time and which amendments can be offered, and it sets aside certain procedural objections. The House adopted it on June 24, 2025.
for: Supporters say it lets the House move quickly on funding for veterans and military bases and on border security measures, with set time for debate and a list of allowed amendments.
against: Critics say it restricts amendments and waives procedural protections, limiting debate on immigration measures with serious consequences for the people affected.
